title: Effect of placebo on exercise response and nitroglycerin consumption.

screening.rationale: Title indicates an empirical study testing placebo effects on exercise response and nitroglycerin consumption in humans, making placebo the object of study despite no abstract.

classification.summary: Investigated the effect of placebo on exercise tolerance and nitroglycerin use in angina patients, but no abstract or results were available.

title: Double-blind evaluation of intradiscal chymopapain for herniated lumbar discs. Early results.
abstract: The authors report 66 patients with signs, symptoms, and a myelographic abnormality of herniated lumbar disc, who were not responsive to conservative treatment. The discs were injected at random with either chymopapain or a placebo. Neither patient nor surgeon knew which agent was used until after the results had been tabulated. Unless early laminectomy was necessary for intractable pain, all patients were followed for 2 months or more. There was no statistically significant difference in incidence or quality of improvement between the two groups: chymopapain was successful in 58% while placebo was successful in 49% (p = 0.15). Early results from this study indicate that most, if not all, of the putative effectiveness of chemonucleolysis probably derives from a placebo effect.

screening.rationale: Randomized placebo-controlled trial that analyzed and interpreted the placebo arm and concluded much of apparent benefit derived from a placebo effect.

classification.summary: Randomized double-blind trial of intradiscal chymopapain versus placebo in 66 patients with herniated lumbar disc found no statistically significant difference between groups, and authors interpreted most apparent benefit as a placebo effect.
classification.key_finding: Chymopapain success 58% vs placebo 49% (p=0.15), suggesting no clear drug advantage and substantial placebo response.

title: Personality correlates of placebo responsivity and religiosity.

screening.rationale: Title and MeSH terms indicate the study empirically examined placebo responsivity as an object of study (personality correlates), meeting the placebo_response inclusion criterion.

classification.summary: Examined personality correlates of placebo responsivity and religiosity in adolescent and adult participants.

title: Cognitive dissonance in the placebo treatment of insomnia -- a pilot experiment.
journal: The British journal of medical psychology
abstract: Insomnia in 11 general hospital in-patients was treated by a placebo. The conditions of administration of the placebo were experimentally varied, and a hypothesis derived from Festinger's cognitive dissonance theory was tested. Consistent with this hypothesis, it was found that patients who were required to make meaningful decisions concerning their treatment derived significantly greater hypnotic (therapeutic) value from it than did patients whose treatment was simply administered to them and who were not required to make such decisions. The power of cognitive dissonance theory to explain the placebo effect, and the therapeutic potential of this approach are discussed.

screening.rationale: Empirical pilot experiment that manipulated conditions of placebo administration to test cognitive dissonance effects on insomnia, meeting inclusion as a placebo/context causal effect study.

classification.summary: Treated 11 hospital in-patients with insomnia using a placebo and experimentally varied administration: those required to make meaningful treatment decisions reported greater hypnotic benefit than those given treatment without choice.
classification.key_finding: Patients who made meaningful decisions about their placebo treatment reported significantly greater subjective hypnotic benefit than patients who received the placebo without choice.

title: Principal aspects of the use of placebos.
abstract: After a brief historical review the author discusses the use of placebo in treatment and in the scientific evaluation of the efficacy of psychotropic drugs in double-blind studies. He also mentions its place in the elucidation of the personality structure and psychodynamics of so-called placebo reactors, as well as its importance in recent years for basic medical research.

screening.rationale: Narrative discussion focused on the use, history, and methodological/clinical role of placebos, making placebo science the main subject.

classification.summary: Reviewed the history and roles of placebos in treatment, psychotropic drug trials, personality/psychodynamic study of placebo reactors, and basic medical research.

title: Conditioned EEG desynchronization and seizure occurrence in patients.
abstract: Five patients with seizures poorly controlled by standard anticonvulsant medication, underwent EEG operant conditioning. The operant paradigm reinforced the production of low voltage fast activity while decreasing frequencies below 10 c/sec. Seizure frequency decreased in 2 patients, seizure severity was attenuated in 2 others, and one patient who was only given reinforecement for scalp EMG suppression whowed no change in seizure parameters. Pseudoconditioning and control periods ruled out placebo effects. A rationale for this phenomenon is proposed.

screening.rationale: Human empirical study tested operant EEG conditioning effects on seizure frequency/severity with control/pseudoconditioning periods, addressing conditioned contextual/learning mechanisms relevant to placebo science.

classification.summary: Tested operant EEG conditioning (neurofeedback) in five medicated epilepsy patients and found reductions in seizure frequency or severity in four patients, with pseudoconditioning and control periods used to rule out placebo effects.
classification.key_finding: Seizure frequency decreased in 2 patients and seizure severity was attenuated in 2 others following reinforcement of low-voltage fast EEG patterns.

title: Pharmacotherapy with avena sativa - a double blind study.
journal: International journal of clinical pharmacology and biopharmacy
abstract: Hundred non-hospitalized smokers with an average consumption of 20 cigarettes per day were treated with an alcoholic extract of Avena sativa for disaccustoming. The study was double blind. By using query-sheets personal contact was excluded. The first result was a placebo-effect of 35% for disaccustoming of smokers and no statistically significant effect of the extract of Avena sativa. The second result was a difference of disaccustoming between light and heavy smokers. It was shown, that the rate of disaccustoming was higher for light smokers than for smokers with a high consumption of cigarettes.

screening.rationale: Randomized double-blind trial that reported and analyzed a 35% placebo-effect (placebo-arm response) for smoking cessation, so the placebo response was an object of study.

classification.summary: Found a 35% placebo-effect for smoking cessation and no statistically significant benefit of Avena sativa; light smokers quit at higher rates than heavy smokers.
classification.key_finding: Placebo-arm quit rate was 35%; Avena sativa showed no significant advantage.

title: The effects of cerebral electric therapy (electrosleep) on anxiety, depression, and hostility in psychiatric patients.
journal: The Journal of nervous and mental disease
abstract: The effects of cerebral electric therapy (electrosleep) and placebo on self-ratings of anxiety, depression, and hostility were compared. No difference in the amount of improvement shown by the two groups appeared on any of the five measures employed, although a major placebo effect was evident on all of the criteria. The results argue against the use of electrosleep as a treatment for these symptoms except when it may be employed for its placebo value.

screening.rationale: Controlled clinical trial reported large improvements in the placebo arm and discussed the placebo value, so placebo response was a substantive object of analysis.

classification.summary: Compared electrosleep to a placebo sham and found no difference, with large improvements observed in the placebo group on self-rated anxiety, depression, and hostility.
classification.key_finding: Found no superiority of electrosleep over placebo; placebo group showed major subjective improvement across measures.

title: The power of suggestion: another examination of misattribution and insomnia.
journal: Journal of personality and social psychology
abstract: This experiment was conducted in an attempt to replicate and delimit the reverse placebo effect found by Storms and Nisbett in insomniacs. It was predicted that the reverse placebo effect would obtain when the pills' effects were described as affecting arousal (as in Storms and Nisbett's study) but that a direct suggestion effect would result when the pills were described as directly affecting sleep onset latency. Results indicated that direct suggestion effects obtained regardless of the focus of the instructions. The present study together with the findings of Kellogg and Baron call into question the reliability and clinical significance of the reverse placebo effect in the treatment of insomnia.

screening.rationale: Empirical experiment that manipulated suggestion/placebo instructions to examine placebo (reverse placebo) and direct suggestion effects on insomnia outcomes.

classification.summary: Conducted an experiment in insomniacs manipulating pill instructions and found direct suggestion effects on sleep onset latency regardless of instruction focus, questioning the reliability of the reverse placebo effect.
classification.key_finding: Found that direct verbal suggestion reduced sleep onset latency (subjective) irrespective of whether pills were described as affecting arousal or sleep.

title: Disulfiram implantation: placebo, psychological deterrent, and pharmacological deterrent effects.
journal: The British journal of psychiatry : the journal of mental science
abstract: In an effort to examine the placebo, psychological deterrent, and pharmacological deterrent effects associated with implanted disulfiram, subjects were given either disulfiram implants or sham operations. Ethanol challenges elicited no disulfiram-ethanol reactions (DERs), indicating that at the time of the challenge neither a pharmacological deterrent nor a placebo effect was operating. Of the patients who resumed drinking, only those with disulfiram implants experienced DERs. Sham operation subjects continued to drink after their first post-challenge drink; four of five disulfiram implant recidivists remained abstinent following their experience of a DER. It is concluded that the pharmacological deterrent effect of the disulfiram implant may have been underestimated in previous reports.

screening.rationale: Controlled clinical trial directly compared disulfiram implants to sham operations to examine placebo/psychological and pharmacological deterrent effects.

classification.summary: Compared disulfiram implants versus sham operations in alcohol-dependent patients and found implants produced disulfiram-ethanol reactions and reduced subsequent drinking, whereas sham subjects continued to drink after challenge.
classification.key_finding: Only patients with disulfiram implants experienced DERs and some remained abstinent after DERs, suggesting a pharmacological deterrent effect.

title: Evoked potentials in hyperkinetic and normal children under certainty and uncertainty: a placebo and methylphenidate study.

screening.rationale: No abstract available and title/MeSH indicate a placebo-controlled methylphenidate evoked-potential study, but it's unclear whether placebo/nocebo effects or placebo responses were an object of study rather than serving only as a control.

classification.summary: Insufficient abstract; reported comparisons of evoked potentials in hyperkinetic and normal children involving placebo and methylphenidate under certainty versus uncertainty, but whether placebo effects/responses were analyzed is unclear.

title: Issues at the clinical-research interface: placebo effect control groups.
journal: The Journal of nervous and mental disease
abstract: At the clinical-research interface, controls are a significant issue in group therapy evaluation. The authors describe and analyze their unique experience with placebo effect control groups conducted prior to brief, group psychotherapy for married couples. Procedures are outlined and participant reactions noted. Solicited ratings and spontaneous comments provide assessment data. The evidence suggests the feasibility of placebo effect control groups in the context studied. Proposed methodological refinements and clinical implications may be useful for future research efforts.

screening.rationale: Paper empirically described and analyzed the use of placebo-effect control groups in group psychotherapy, addressing placebo methodology at the clinical-research interface.

classification.summary: Described and analyzed the authors' experience implementing placebo-effect control groups before brief group psychotherapy for married couples, reporting participant reactions and methodological recommendations.
classification.key_finding: Found that placebo-effect control groups were feasible in this group psychotherapy context and proposed procedural refinements.

title: Comparison of muscle relaxation with placebo medication for anxiety reduction in alcoholic inpatients.
journal: Current therapeutic research, clinical and experimental

screening.rationale: No abstract available; title describes a controlled trial comparing muscle relaxation to a placebo medication in alcoholic inpatients but it is unclear whether the placebo/placebo response was an object of analysis versus serving as a control for the relaxation intervention.

classification.summary: No abstract available; title indicated a controlled trial comparing muscle relaxation versus placebo medication for anxiety reduction in alcoholic inpatients.

title: Small bowel motility: comparison of the effects of an anticholinergic agent, this agent plus a tranquilizer, and a placebo.
journal: Current therapeutic research, clinical and experimental

screening.rationale: No abstract or full text provided to determine whether the placebo arm was analyzed as an object of study versus serving only as a comparator in a drug efficacy trial.

classification.summary: No abstract available; randomized clinical trial from 1976 that compared an anticholinergic, the agent plus a tranquilizer, and a placebo on small-bowel motility, with insufficient information to judge whether placebo effects were analyzed.

title: The effect of measuring error on the results of therapeutic trials in advanced cancer.
abstract: In this study, 16 experienced oncologists each measured 12 simulated tumor masses employing their usual clinical methods. Unknown to the oncologists, two pairs of these tumors were identical in size. This permitted a total of 64 measurement comparisons of the same investigator measuring the same size mass and 1920 comparisons of different investigators measuring the same size mass. If a 50% reduction in the product of perpendicular diameters is accepted as a criterion, the objective response rate due to measuring error alone was 7.8% by the same investigator and 6.8% by different investigators. If a 25% reduction criterion is used, the respective "placebo" response rates were 19% and 25%. In the clinical setting it is recommended that the 50% reduction criterion be employed and that the investigator should anticipate an objective response rate of 5 to 10% due to human error in tumor measurement.

screening.rationale: Empirical study examined how measurement error produced spurious objective 'placebo' response rates, addressing trial methodology and placebo response measurement.

classification.summary: Measured how oncologist measurement error produced apparent tumor 'responses', finding nontrivial false response rates depending on response criteria.
classification.key_finding: Measurement error produced apparent objective response rates of about 6.8–25% depending on the percent-reduction criterion (50% vs 25%).

title: Letter: Continued need for placebos.
journal: The British journal of psychiatry : the journal of mental science

screening.rationale: Journal letter explicitly about the need for placebos and research design, so placebo is the main subject (editorial/letter)

classification.summary: Argued for the continued importance of placebo controls and consideration of placebo use in clinical research and design.

title: An evaluation of the double-blind design in a study comparing lithium carbonate with placebo.
abstract: As part of a study of drug treatment of aggressive behavior to be reported separately, we have evaluated the double-blind procedure in a recently completed comparison of the efficacy of lithium carbonate versus placebo in modifying aggressive behavior in nonpsychotic incarcerated delinquents. We conclude that the side effects of lithium carbonate are sufficient to reveal the medication to most subjects receiving it. Thus, while the study staff could not identify lithium-receivers at better than chance levels, and while subjects who received placebo could not identify their medication at better than chance levels, subjects who received lithium could accurately identify it. On a weekly symptom check list there was no difference between lithium and placebo groups on average lithium target symptoms reported during 4-week pre- and postmedication control periods; however, lithium-receivers reported significantly more target symptoms every week medication was administered. Of 16 subjects who quit the study, 14 had received lithium and nearly all of those who gave reasons for quitting specified side effects, most often nausea. The methodological problems of using lithium in a double-blind design might be overcome by employing a "discontinuation" design, or, speculatively, a double-blind, cross-over design utilizing an "active placebo".

screening.rationale: Paper empirically evaluated double-blind integrity and placebo-related methodological issues (unblinding due to side effects), meeting inclusion for placebo science/trial methodology.

classification.summary: Evaluated double-blind integrity in a lithium-versus-placebo trial in incarcerated delinquents and found lithium recipients often identified their medication from side effects and disproportionately quit the study.
classification.key_finding: Subjects receiving lithium accurately identified their medication due to side effects (commonly nausea), and most dropouts occurred in the lithium group.

title: Guest Editorial: Let's use the placebo.
mesh: Education of Persons with Intellectual Disabilities

screening.rationale: Title and MeSH terms explicitly reference placebos and physician–patient relations, indicating the editorial's main subject was placebo use.

classification.summary: Argued for using placebos in clinical care and discussed physician–patient relations and education concerning people with intellectual disabilities.

title: Acupuncture for chronic shoulder pain. An experimental study with attention to the role of placebo and hypnotic susceptibility.
abstract: One half of 42 subjects treated for painful shoulders received classic acupuncture, and one half received a placebo in which the needles did not penetrate the skin. Half of each of these groups was treated in a positive setting to encourage the subject, and half in a negative setting designed to keep encouragement at a minimum. All patients were independently rated for susceptibility to hypnosis. Although range of motion did not improve, the majority of patients reported significant improvement in shoulder discomfort to a blind evaluator after treatment; placebo and acupuncture groups did not differ in this respect, however. The positive and negative settings did not affect treatment outcome. In all groups, those who were not rated as highly susceptible to hypnosis tended to fail to achieve the highest levels of relief, but such differences were not statistically significant.

screening.rationale: Randomized trial directly compared penetrating acupuncture with a nonpenetrating (placebo) sham and manipulated treatment context, making placebo effects and contextual moderators the study's focus.

classification.summary: Randomized trial of penetrating versus nonpenetrating (placebo) acupuncture for chronic shoulder pain manipulated positive versus negative treatment setting and measured hypnotic susceptibility; found similar self-reported improvement in both real and sham acupuncture and no effect on range of motion or setting.
classification.key_finding: No difference between real and sham acupuncture on patient-reported shoulder discomfort; treatment context manipulation did not alter outcomes.

title: Sequential withdrawal of stimulant drugs and use of behavior therapy with two hyperactive boys.
abstract: The separate and combined effects of stimulant drugs, placebos, and behavior therapy were investigated with two hyperactive boys. In each case, sequential replacement of drugs (Ritalin and Dexedrine) with placebos demonstrated placebo effects of the drugs; behavior therapy, alone and in combination with drugs, was effective in controlling hyperactive behaviors. Implications in regard to drugs as treatment of choice are discussed.

screening.rationale: Case-report experiment sequentially replaced stimulant drugs with placebo and reported placebo effects on hyperactive behavior, meeting inclusion for placebo effect research.

classification.summary: Reported two case studies in which sequential replacement of stimulant medications with placebo produced observable reductions in hyperactive behaviors, and behavior therapy was also effective.
classification.key_finding: Placebo substitution produced behavioral improvements indicative of placebo effects of stimulant medications in both cases.

title: Personality factors and drug effects in a controlled study of cyclazocine.
abstract: This paper investigated the relationship between measurable personality factors and level of effects shown to cyclazocine and placebo in a controlled study. An attempt also was made through case analysis to examine the association between dynamic aspects of personality and adverse drug effect. Hysteria scores on the MMPI were found to be related significantly to self-reported effects under both the drug and placebo conditions. Clinical observations were examined retrospectively for three cases with adverse reactions and cited to support a dynamic theory that associated drug reactivity to personality factors.

screening.rationale: Controlled clinical trial explicitly analyzed effects under both drug and placebo and related placebo responses to personality factors, meeting inclusion for placebo/placebo-response research.

classification.summary: Investigated personality factors and effects of cyclazocine and placebo in a controlled clinical study and found MMPI hysteria scores were significantly related to self-reported effects under both drug and placebo, with case analyses linking personality to adverse reactions.
classification.key_finding: MMPI hysteria scores correlated with greater self-reported responses to both cyclazocine and placebo, suggesting personality influenced placebo and drug reactivity.

title: Levoamphetamine vs dextroamphetamine in minimal brain dysfunction. Replication, time response, and differential effect by diagnostic group and family rating.
abstract: Double-blind crossover randomized Latin square comparison of placebo, dextroamphetamine, and levoamphetamine in 31 consecutively diagnosed children with minimal brain dysfunction (MBD) replicated a smaller nonrandom study. Both isomers showed significantly more benefit than placebo but were not significantly different from each other. Dextroamphetamine showed a nonsignificant trend of superiority over levoamphetamine. Of 25 subjects who responded well to drugs, three responded only to levoamphetamine, five only to dextroamphetamine, and 17 to both. This study seems to confirm the efficacy of levoamphetamine in MBD. An unsocialized aggressive subgroup (308.4) showed a nonsignificant trend for levoamphetamine superiority, in contrast to the hyperkinetic (308.0) and overanxious (308.2) subgroups. Those who responded best to levoamphetamine tended (not significantly) to be from poorer functioning families. Parents' ratings, but not teachers' or psychiatrists' ratings, showed significant placebo effect.

screening.rationale: Randomized double-blind crossover trial reported a significant placebo effect on parent ratings, so placebo/placebo-response was analyzed rather than serving only as an incidental comparator.

classification.summary: Randomized double-blind crossover trial in 31 children compared placebo, dextro- and levoamphetamine and found both isomers superior to placebo, with parents' ratings (but not teachers' or psychiatrists') showing a significant placebo effect.
classification.key_finding: Parents' ratings showed a significant placebo effect while teachers' and psychiatrists' did not; both amphetamine isomers outperformed placebo (N=31).

title: Letter: Ethics of the placebo.

screening.rationale: Substantive letter in a medical journal whose main topic is the ethics of placebo use, fitting inclusion for placebo_science_other (ethics/clinical use).

classification.summary: Discusses the ethical issues surrounding placebo use and physician–patient relations in clinical practice.

title: Who responds to sugar pills?
abstract: Among 288 cancer patients undergoing controlled trials of oral analgesics there were 112 who received 50% or greater pain relief from placebo formulations. Patients who responded to placebo had a greater response rate to active drugs. They also had a higher incidence of central nervous system side effects to placebo. Patient groups showing as increased placebo response included those with a high level of education, farmers, those with a professional occupation, women working outside the home, and patients who were widowed, separated, or divorced. Those resistant to placebo were patients with a low educational level, unskilled workers, housewives, married women without children, and smokers. It is theorized that placebo response is a type of autohypnosis phenomenon resulting from exaggerated oral-dependency needs. Particularly vulnerable to placebo effect is the very self-sufficient individual with heavy responsibilities who is thrust into the unaccustomed dependency of disabling illness.

screening.rationale: Analyzed placebo-arm responders and predictors within analgesic trials, so placebo response was the object of study (placebo_arm_secondary_analysis).

classification.summary: Analyzed 288 cancer patients from analgesic trials and found 112 had ≥50% pain relief on placebo; responders were more likely to respond to active drugs and report CNS side effects.
classification.key_finding: Found 112/288 (~39%) achieved ≥50% pain relief on placebo; placebo responders showed higher active-drug response rates and more CNS side effects.

title: A bitter pill to swallow: placebo therapy in general practice.

screening.rationale: Title and MeSH terms indicate the paper addresses placebo therapy and physician–patient relations in general practice, meeting inclusion for placebo science (ethics/clinical use/attitudes), despite no abstract.

classification.summary: Discusses placebo therapy in general practice, focusing on physician–patient relations and the sociological aspects of placebo prescribing.

title: Do placebos alter sleep?
abstract: Deliberate suggestion that an inert capsule was a sleeping pill was found not to influence subjective ratings of sleep quality or anxiety or the electrophysiologically recorded features of sleep in 10 volunteers aged 41-62 years.

screening.rationale: Empirical controlled trial that directly tested whether suggestion that an inert capsule was a sleeping pill altered subjective and electrophysiological sleep outcomes, so it studies a placebo effect.

classification.summary: Tested whether suggesting an inert capsule was a sleeping pill altered subjective sleep quality or electrophysiological sleep measures in 10 middle-aged volunteers and found no effect.
classification.key_finding: No change in subjective sleep quality or EEG-recorded sleep features with suggestion of an inert sleeping pill.

title: A double-blind comparative study of the analgesic effects of fenbufen, codeine, aspirin, propoxyphene and placebo.
journal: Current therapeutic research, clinical and experimental

screening.rationale: No abstract or results available to determine whether the placebo arm or placebo effects/responses were analyzed versus being only a comparator in an analgesic efficacy trial.

classification.summary: Reported a double-blind randomized comparative trial of fenbufen, codeine, aspirin, propoxyphene and placebo for postoperative analgesia; abstract/results not available to judge placebo-specific analyses.

title: A comparison of the effects of salbutamol, fenoterol, and placebo aerosols on airway resistance in asthmatics.

screening.rationale: Randomized trial with a placebo arm but no abstract or full text to show whether placebo/nocebo effects or placebo-arm responses were analyzed or discussed.

classification.summary: Reported a randomized comparison of salbutamol, fenoterol, and placebo aerosols on airway resistance in asthmatic adults, but no abstract/full text was available to assess analyses of placebo effects or responses.

title: On the choice of so-called placebo solution for the intranigral microinjection in the rat.
journal: Polish journal of pharmacology and pharmacy
abstract: Rats moving freely in their cages were injected into substantia nigra with bidistilled water, with NaCl solutions of various concentrations or with a multionic Merle's solution. The solutions were administered uni- or bilaterally at volumes of 1-5 mul through chronically implanted chemitrodes. The behavior of animals and the EEG of frontal cortex, hippocampus, caudate nucleus and substantia nigra were observed. A part of the usual EEG record analysis two channels of EEG were evaluated with amplitude integrators. The main goal of the experiment was to find the optimal solvent for microinjection into the substantia nigra. So-called physiological saline solution (0-9% NaCl) was found to be most toxic and the multionic Merle's solution most suitable among the control fluids tested. The influence of "pressing effect", of pH as well as the influence of ionic concentrations of solutions tested are discussed.

screening.rationale: Animal experiment that directly tested different inert control solutions (placebo vehicles) and their causal effects on behavior and EEG, so placebo/control fluid choice was the object of study.

classification.summary: Compared bidistilled water, various NaCl concentrations and a multionic Merle's solution for intranigral microinjection in rats and found physiological and behavioral differences, with 0.9% saline most toxic and Merle's solution most suitable.
classification.key_finding: Found 0.9% NaCl (physiological saline) produced the most toxic effects on behavior and EEG, while multionic Merle's solution was most suitable as a control fluid.

title: Panel III: Psychological aspects, placebo effect and rehabilitation methodology. Discussion.

screening.rationale: Title explicitly addresses placebo effect and rehabilitation methodology in a panel discussion, making placebo a main subject despite missing abstract.

classification.summary: Panel discussion considered psychological aspects, the placebo effect, and rehabilitation methodology in coronary disease and post-myocardial infarction care.

title: Panel III: Pyschological aspects, placebo effect and rehabilitation methodology.

screening.rationale: Title explicitly names placebo effect and rehabilitation methodology but no abstract or full text was available to determine whether it presents empirical data or is a conceptual/panel discussion.

classification.summary: Discusses psychological aspects, the placebo effect, and rehabilitation methodology in patients with coronary disease and myocardial infarction.

title: Explaining and exploiting placebo effects.

screening.rationale: Title and MeSH terms indicate the article addresses placebo mechanisms and their clinical exploitation, meeting inclusion as placebo science review/theory despite missing abstract.

classification.summary: Reviewed and discussed mechanisms underlying placebo effects and considered ways to exploit them clinically.

title: Subjective ratings of sleep quality and anxiety after placebo, drug and a food drink.
abstract: Ten subjects (mean age 57 years) took part in a crossover study between a food drink and nitrazepam 5 mg. They rated their anxiety and sleep quality. On half the sleep laboratory nights during baseline periods subjects were given an inert pill which they were told would improve sleep. A comparison was made between the six pill and six non-pill nights for each subject. Subjective ratings revealed no significant difference attributable to the inert pill. Sleep quality was rated to have been improved during both late drug and early food drink administration. On early drug withdrawal sleep quality was rated worse than baseline.

screening.rationale: Within-subject comparison of inert pill (told it would improve sleep) versus non-pill nights directly tested placebo effect on subjective sleep and anxiety.

classification.summary: Conducted a crossover within-subject study (n=10, mean age 57) comparing inert pill nights versus non-pill nights and found no significant subjective improvement in sleep or anxiety attributable to the inert pill.
classification.key_finding: No reliable placebo effect on self-reported sleep quality or anxiety was observed (pill vs non-pill nights).

title: Gastro-intestinal microbleeding under acetylsalicylic acid, ketoprofen and placebo.
abstract: A quantitative comparison of gastro-intestinal microbleeding induced by acetylsalicylic acid (ASA), 3.6 g daily, ketoprofen (KETO), 200 mg daily and placebo (P) was undertaken in 12 normal volunteers using a double-blind factorial design with repeated measures. We conclude that KETO induces less gastro-intestinal bleeding than ASA but more than placebo and that there is a significant residual bleeding under placebo following ASA.

screening.rationale: Controlled double-blind repeated-measures trial that reported and analyzed bleeding observed in the placebo arm (residual bleeding following ASA), making the placebo response an object of analysis.

classification.summary: Randomized double-blind factorial repeated-measures trial in 12 healthy volunteers compared ASA, ketoprofen, and placebo and found ketoprofen caused less gastrointestinal microbleeding than ASA but more than placebo, with residual bleeding observed under placebo after ASA.
classification.key_finding: Found that ketoprofen produced less GI microbleeding than aspirin but more than placebo, and that placebo measurements after aspirin showed significant residual bleeding.

title: Sustained-release lithium carbonate in double-blind study: serum lithium levels, side effects, and placebo response.
abstract: The utility and side effects of sustained-release lithium carbonate (Priadel) in a once-per-day dose regimen was investigated with 66 male delinquents, ages 17-24 years, in a double-blind study comparing the antiaggressive effect of lithium carbonate with placebo. Serum lithium levels and symptoms were determined weekly for up to eight drug-free and 12 on-medication weeks. Average daily doses of 1500-1700 mg Priadel gave 24-hour serum lithium levels in the range 0.7-0.9 mEq/liter. Principal side effects were polyuria and shakiness, with other important side effects bring hand tremor, dryness of mouth, nausea, and weakness. No lithium toxicity was observed, and diarrhea was reported infrequently. Placebo response data are presented.

screening.rationale: Randomized double-blind trial that reported and presented placebo response data, so placebo response was an object of analysis rather than merely a comparator.

classification.summary: Randomized double-blind trial of sustained-release lithium versus placebo in 66 male delinquents (ages 17–24) that measured serum levels, side effects, and presented placebo-response data.

title: Credibility ratings for desensitization and pseudotherapy among moderately and mildly snake-avoidant college students.
abstract: Twenty moderately avoidant and 20 mildly avoidant Ss were chosen as though they were to participate in a snake-avoidance desensitization experiment. After relaxation training, Ss listened to a taped excerpt of either desensitization or pseudotherapy and responded to a 5-item questionnaire that assessed the credibility of the treatment. Mildly avoidant Ss rated desensitization as more credible than pseudotherapy. The implication of this finding is that a great many experimental studies of systematic desensitization have failed to control satisfactorily for the operation of expectancy effects and nonspecific forms of behavioral influence.

screening.rationale: Empirical study experimentally manipulated treatment script (desensitization vs pseudotherapy) and measured expectancy/credibility, addressing placebo-related nonspecific/contextual effects.

classification.summary: Found that mildly snake-avoidant college students rated a taped desensitization treatment as more credible than a pseudotherapy tape, implying expectancy and nonspecific influences on desensitization studies.
classification.key_finding: Mildly avoidant participants rated desensitization as more credible than pseudotherapy (n=40).
